correctness.rationale: For y=p^v u, p∤u, a positive inverse must be x=p^a m with m prime to p. The valuation equation is a−1+ν_p(a)=v; its unit equation b_a m=u gives one inverse exactly when b_a|u. Thus i_p(y)=Σ_{a∈A_{p,v}}1_{b_a|u}. For each fixed v, CRT residues modulo prime-to-p lcms produce the exact indicator expansion P_{p,v}(z). The omitted v>V mass is p^{−V−1}, proving the limiting coefficient law and normalization, not merely finite testing. A nonnegative rearrangement gives the mean (p−1)Σ_{a≥1}1/(ap^a)=(p−1)log(p/(p−1)); at most one a per ν_p(a) yields the double-exponential-in-r tail bound. Positivity at r=0 uses the empty stratum v=p−1 and at r≥1 uses Emmons–Xiao Theorem21 witness plus a positive-density congruence class. Independently enumerated every y≤1100 and conditional PGFs for v≤12 at p=2,3,5; all matched. Finite checks are corroboration, and the asserted all-prime limit follows from the above proof, including p=2 and the v=0 boundary.
residual_risks: The unconditional positivity for every positive multiplicity depends on the accurately cited external constructive existence theorem (verified statement and proof).
Numerical densities require their stated rigorous truncation, not numerical floating-point equality.

value.rationale: The distribution of inverse multiplicities for a natural prime arithmetic derivative is itself an independently useful quantitative invariant. Existence of individual inverse counts was known, whereas the effective all-count density law, explicitly bounded approximation, exact first moment and strong tail are structurally motivated global results. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or a mere new notation for the prior theorem.
residual_risks: The law is specialized to positive integer inverse images of D_p, and individual density constants have no claimed elementary closed forms.
